transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

When I have to sit and focus on these long claim files, my mind just checks out and I end up putting them off or staring at the screen instead of getting them done. It's really starting to cause problems for me at my job, and I just can't seem to keep up anymore.
Have you had similar problems with inattention or distractibility since childhood or in more than one setting, such as at home, school, or in other jobs?

Yes, this actually goes back to when I was a kid. In elementary school, teachers always wrote on my report cards that I was daydreaming, losing worksheets, or forgetting to turn in homework. I managed to get through high school and college by cramming at the last minute and relying on a good memory, so it never really drew formal attention until now.
Do you also have problems with being unusually fidgety, restless, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly trouble with attention and organization?

I actually do struggle with some restlessness and fidgeting quite a bit. I find myself constantly bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, or shifting around in my chair at my desk. During long meetings, I even find excuses to get up and walk around because I feel too antsy to just sit still.
Do you also tend to act or speak before thinking, such as interrupting people, blurting out answers, or making impulsive decisions that you later regret?

No, I don't really struggle with those specific issues. I don't typically interrupt people, blurt out answers, or make impulsive decisions. My main difficulties are really more about staying focused, keeping organized, and dealing with that physical restlessness.
Do these attention and restlessness problems cause difficulties in more than one area of your life, such as at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yes, it's causing major issues at work where I've been written up twice, missed a promotion, and constantly worry about getting fired. It also spills into my personal life with things like forgetting dentist appointments, and looking back, it definitely caused trouble in school when I was younger with daydreaming and losing homework.
Do you often act on impulse, such as interrupting people, blurting out answers, or making hasty decisions you later regret?

No, I don't really experience issues with impulsivity, interrupting others, or making hasty decisions. My struggles are definitely much more about staying focused on my work and keeping things organized.
Do you find that these symptoms were present before age 12, and have they continued consistently into adulthood?

Yes, they definitely started before age 12; back in elementary school, my teachers always wrote on my report cards about me daydreaming, losing worksheets, and forgetting homework. Although I managed to get by in high school and college by cramming, these issues have persisted and became a major obstacle over the last 15 months with my new workload.
Do you also have symptoms like feeling internally restless, needing to move around, or being unable to relax even when you want to sit still?

Yes, I definitely feel that way. When sitting at my desk, I'm constantly bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, and shifting around in my chair because I feel too restless if I try to stop. During long team meetings, I get so antsy that I'll get up to grab water or use the restroom even when I don't actually need to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/restlessness beginning before age 12, present in more than one setting (school, work, home), and causing clear occupational and functional impairment. Impulsivity is denied, but the confirmed symptoms meet the presentation consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive with hyperactive/restless features; among the provided options, F90.0 is the best fit.
